By 2030, data centers alone could consume up to 3–5% of global electricity; placing immense pressure on power systems, water resources, and infrastructure, especially in regions already managing constrained resources.
 
In response, countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America are advancing regional, scalable, climate-smart pathways that the rest of the world can learn from:
 
🌐 In the SIJORI Growth Triangle (Singapore–Johor–Riau), cross-border compute sharing is helping to bridge infrastructure gaps and unlock regional AI innovation efficiently and affordably.
 
🌐 In Kenya, a clear geothermal policy attracted development finance, enabling Microsoft and a UAE partner to build a geothermal-powered data center - a scalable model for clean, resilient AI infrastructure in East Africa.
 
🌐 In Cambodia, Myanmar, and Laos, countries are exploring regional compute models to tap into underused capacity - scaling AI access without overloading national grids or diverting limited budgets.
 
The Global South is not just participating in the AI transition; it’s actively shaping how AI is built, powered, and governed to reflect the realities of people and communities themselves.
